To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the isolated neutron star RX J0806-4123 is a radio pulsar, that its radio emission is highly linearly polarized, and that its spin frequency is 0.5 Hz, i.e. the rotation period is 2.0 s.

1) the X-ray spectra of the isolated neutron stars RX J0420 and RX J0803 are consistent with the thermal emission from the surface of neutron stars; 2) the optical counterparts of these sources have a very low extinction and are consistent with being the same objects as those seen in X-rays; and 3) the optical and X-ray data can be fitted with a single temperature blackbody model.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (1) The study of the physical processes of the neutron star (NS) surface emission, (2) The study of NS magnetic fields and the NS magnetic field decay, (3) The study of pulsar wind nebulae (PWNe) and the interaction of the PWNe with their environment, and (4) The study of supernova remnants.
the study of isolated neutron stars (INSs) discovered in the X-ray band, with the aim of characterizing their emission mechanisms and the properties of their surrounding environments.
the development and application of a new class of neutron star equations of state (EOSs), the so-called hyperon EOSs.
